updates.rationale: Without access, an auxiliary-receiver converse is a plausible but non-default program. Direct effort covers identifying the route, screening applicable public theorems, coordinating the specialization, and checking that the optimization order is preserved before the withheld conditions are independently established.

Independent discovery requires a substantial agenda-setting and literature-search effort to recognize that an imported auxiliary-receiver theorem may specialize to the private-message task and to separate useful premises from irrelevant common-message machinery.

Once this program is pursued, the specialization is a core work package. A researcher must reconstruct the finite constraint model, remove the common-message coordinate, verify the receiver reduction, retain the nested optimization order, and certify the resulting private-rate ceiling without relying on the withheld contribution.

The route has a sizable fallback burden from unsuccessful theorem matches, alternative receiver couplings, invalid exchanges of optimization order, and failed specializations. The estimate is calibrated to the existing unstructured converse-search packages while allowing additional effort for independently locating the relevant premise.
